name: STEPHEN ADEYEMI ADEJINMI
feedback: On D1 this is a near-complete catalogue and it is excellent work. All ten findings are present, each with a correct OWASP class, a correct CWE, the login.php line range, the capture timestamp, and a short quoted code fragment: SQLi A03/CWE-89 at login.php 64 to 67 reconciled to 02:15:31, alg:none A07/CWE-347 with the if alg none return payload branch, the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 with no exp/nbf, unsalted MD5 CWE-916, cookie flags CWE-614/1004, open redirect CWE-601 at 02:21:13, stored XSS CWE-79 at 02:18:47 with the cookie beacon, XXE CWE-611 with file:///etc/passwd, and path traversal CWE-22 at 02:24:02. The decoy is nailed: you name the hash_equals HS256 verify branch, prove it safe at the mechanism level as a constant-time comparison, and explicitly separate it from the real bugs which are alg:none and the hardcoded secret, so you avoided the trap of mislabelling alg:none the decoy. Full marks here. On D2 the chain is in order and every hop from recon through file read is reconciled to a capture line, the verbatim PoC payloads are present per hop, and the impact analysis is strong: 312 customers, a naira range with stated assumptions, a central estimate of about N63 million, all tied to the BoltCash context. The one thing that cost you is the F-01 CVSS vector. You scored it 10.0 with S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H, and while S:C is defensible through the shared /api/v1/internal scope change, the A:H is wrong: the auth bypass does not touch availability, so the correct vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, or 9.6 if you keep S:C, and not A:H. Fix the availability metric and that row is perfect. On D3 the report is tied to evidence throughout, the threat model reads the Tor operator as methodical recon rather than a scanner, the decoy is disproved correctly, the earliest-break fix is the network block of /legacy-admin which you correctly argue eliminates all ten findings for an afternoon of effort, and crucially your remediation table is ordered by Risk Reduced Per Hour of Effort rather than CVSS severity, which is exactly what the rubric rewards. Both detection stopgaps give exact log fields and false-positive rates. The only soft spot is that the executive summary still leans on terms like stored injection and session-harvest script without a plain-language gloss, even though it does land on the N63 million headline, so translate those for a non-technical board reader next time. On D4 you answer all four prompts in a clear first-person voice, you cite ISC2 Canon I by number as load-bearing for overriding the manager, you name NDPA 2023 Section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and reach Section 41 for data-subject notice, and you tie both to the 312 customers, and the whole thing is anchored to your own findings at about 420 words. The single most important fix is the F-01 CVSS vector: change A:H to A:N so the flagship score reflects that an auth bypass does not degrade availability.
